clue.text: Most blows come with it

parts.note: read 'blows' as gusts of air rather than punches: the most common breeze in a region arrives from this direction

explanation.definitionFit: The usual direction from which the air moves in an area is the one most gusts come from.

clue.text: Triangle existing always?

parts.note: the love triangle of fiction is proverbially everlasting, and the adjective in that stock phrase also means lasting for ever

explanation.definitionFit: Something existing for all time is everlasting; the same word completes the stock phrase for a three-way love affair.

clue.text: One accepted new complaint

indicators.note: one piece taking in another is shown by 'accepted', so the first word's letters surround the second

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A single person has taken on a fresh grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition of spots is a medical complaint, in the sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Be taking Italian at university — enjoy oneself

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
IT is crossword shorthand for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
UP means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student studying Italian at college has a great time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for celebrating or having a lavish good time.

clue.text: Number ask for silence having finished feast

parts.note: SH is the sound made to ask people to be quiet
UP means over or finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: Someone calls for quiet once a big meal is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for a large hearty meal, a blowout or banquet.

clue.text: It is not wanted in the basket

definitions.text: It is not wanted in the basket

parts.words: It is not wanted in the basket
parts.note: read not as something unwanted by a shopper but as discarded sheets, which end up in the office bin because nobody wants them

explanation.definitionFit: Discarded sheets and scraps are rubbish thrown into an office bin.

clue.text: Ran in a vehicle initially travelling in blissful place

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about, so this group is rearranged
initially points to the opening letter of the word vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone drove into an idyllic spot while on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes V from 'vehicle'; 'travelling' rearranges RANINA plus V into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the state of perfect peace, used loosely for any paradise.

clue.text: Parachutist who is shouldn't feel it!

definitions.text: Parachutist who is shouldn't feel it!

parts.words: Parachutist who is shouldn't feel it!
parts.note: the phrase for utter exhaustion also literally describes a skydiver poised to jump, who ought not to feel tired

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means utterly exhausted, yet literally describes someone prepared to fall from a plane.

clue.text: Bill's partner going to island mountain

parts.note: Bill and Ben were the Flowerpot Men of British children's television
Nevis is a Caribbean island, part of St Kitts and Nevis

explanation.surface: A man's companion heads off to an island with a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben are a pair of puppets from an old British children's TV show, so Bill's partner is BEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish peak is the highest in the British Isles.

clue.text: Worker leaving officer some twilled fabric

indicators.note: a piece leaving another means it is taken away from it

parts.note: a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An employee walks out on their superior, taking a bit of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-wearing woollen cloth woven with diagonal ribs, used for uniforms.

clue.text: One way of ensuring one doesn't have dirty habits

definitions.text: One way of ensuring one doesn't have dirty habits

parts.words: One way of ensuring one doesn't have dirty habits
parts.note: habits here are garments such as a nun's robes, cleaned with solvents rather than water

explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning process using chemical solvents instead of water keeps clothes free of stains.

clue.text: Hurried with Dutch leader's money

parts.note: to have hurried is to have run

indicators.note: a word's leader is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone rushed off with the head of a Dutch firm's cash.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the currency of South Africa.

clue.text: Diminutive worker marking time

parts.note: something diminutive is tiny
a hand is a manual labourer, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A small employee is idling without making progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The long pointer on a clock face shows the passing of the hours' smaller divisions.

clue.text: Plant parts I said intertwine

indicators.note: words that intertwine are twisted together, so their letters get mixed up

explanation.surface: A gardener instructs that sections of a climber should be wound together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intertwine' rearranges the letters of PARTS I SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy foliage houseplant with broad leaves, a fixture of Victorian parlours.

clue.text: Giant firm (American) accepts no profit

indicators.note: one piece accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
having no profit is making a loss

explanation.surface: A huge US company takes on a deficit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant' looks like an adjective for the firm but is the definition; 'accepts' puts the deficit inside the company plus the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge statue, like the one at Rhodes, gives its name to anything enormous.

clue.text: Empty tin in tank

indicators.note: one word placed in another signals that it sits inside it

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
a can is a tin container

explanation.surface: A tin sits unused inside a large container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' and 'tank' both suggest military hardware, but here they are just containers; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Unoccupied or holding nothing, as a room or seat may be.

clue.text: From capital city lady brought pasta

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
Toni is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman has brought back some pasta from a European capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbed tubes of durum wheat are one shape of Italian noodle.

clue.text: Unavoidably involve fifth-rate Latin translation

parts.note: E is the fifth grade, after A to D

indicators.note: a translation changes the form of a text, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy rendering of a classical text is inevitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifth-rate' gives E because grades run from A downwards; 'translation' signals the anagram, which gives NTAIL from the classical language's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To necessitate something is to make it an inevitable consequence.

clue.text: Seat nut removed as result of complaint

indicators.note: letters that are removed are shifted from their places, so this pair of words is rearranged

explanation.surface: A bolt taken out of a chair leads to an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacterial infection causing muscle spasms is a disease, a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: Naive, showing great surprise

definitions.meaning: innocent and credulous, inexperienced in the world
with the eyes opened in astonishment

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both innocently credulous and visibly astonished.

clue.text: Incredibly frosty north, underwear needed!

indicators.note: incredibly suggests something wildly unlike itself, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a freezing northern climate, warm briefs are required.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of men's briefs with an inverted-letter seam at the front.

clue.text: A revolver has been sawn off for the lady

parts.note: a gat is slang for a gun

indicators.note: something sawn off has been cut short, so its last letter is removed

explanation.surface: A handgun has had its barrel cut down for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been sawn off' cuts the last letter from 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's given name, so it stands for a lady.

clue.text: Disturbed night on mat in city

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A restless sleep on the floor in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the English East Midlands, associated with Robin Hood.

clue.text: Craft of golden retriever

parts.note: not a dog's skill: the vessel of Jason, who in Greek myth sailed to fetch the Golden Fleece

explanation.definitionFit: The ship that carried Jason's crew on their quest for the fleece.

clue.text: It could erupt in Vietnam

indicators.note: the letters needed sit in the word Vietnam

explanation.surface: Something in Vietnam could break out at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of a Sicilian volcano is tucked inside 'Vietnam'.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano in Sicily, active and liable to blow.

clue.text: Group performing without safety device

parts.note: no means lacking or without
a net catches acrobats who fall

explanation.surface: A troupe of acrobats is working without a safety net.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical ensemble of nine players.

clue.text: Gently running over the top in town in Hertfordshire

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London

explanation.surface: A jogger goes too far in a Hertfordshire market town.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the container signal; Tring is a small town in Hertfordshire, the county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's pace between walking and cantering, a gentle run.

clue.text: It's the horizon according to my judgement

definitions.meaning: the limit of one's sight, the furthest point visible

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the limit of one's sight and in one's own opinion.
